children: Indonesia's new central bank chief Destry Damayanti said on Wednesday that the rising global bond yields now putting pressure on the country's markets were in line with expectations and would be on the agenda at the bank's next policy meeting.
Destry, 62, made the comments after she was sworn in as the first woman to become the governor of Bank Indonesia.

Previously the bank's senior deputy governor, Destry was the only candidate nominated by President Prabowo Subianto after the surprise resignation in July of predecessor Perry Warjiyo midway through his second term.
Indonesia's 10-year bond yields (ID10YT=RR) rose to 7.229% on Wednesday from 6.990% at the previous day's close, while the rupiah
weakened 0.2% as investors averted risk after renewed U.S. strikes on Iran drove up oil prices and pushed global bond yields to multi-year highs.

"This is in line with our latest assessment. We are indeed facing a 'higher for longer' situation, with high bond yields, high inflation in developed countries and interest rates remaining high," Destry told reporters.

"Global factors will heavily influence the background of our domestic policymaking, and that is something we will continue to pay close attention to," she added, speaking alongside two new members of BI's board of governors, Aida Budiman and Solikin Juhro, who were also sworn in to their new jobs on Wednesday.

Destry takes the helm at a challenging time for Southeast Asia's biggest economy, with investors concerned about fiscal management, stock market transparency and central bank autonomy amid Prabowo's unswerving drive to achieve a high rate of economic growth.
Parliament voted to approve her nomination on Tuesday following her endorsement from its financial committee.
Analysts have said Destry, a Cornell-educated economist, would provide monetary policy continuity and have a good working relationship with the Prabowo administration.
BI raised rates 100 basis points between May and June to defend the rupiah, which has been emerging Asia's worst-performing currency. Its next policy meeting is on September 22 to 23.
